meta.title: Stability from pole location, demonstrated
meta.tools: Impulse responses of systems with poles left of, on and right of the jω axis, growth-rate fitting, BIBO test with a bounded input
meta.summary: Show with worked examples that an LTI system is BIBO-stable exactly when all poles have negative real part: measure the growth rate of impulse responses (it equals the pole's real part), the integrability of |h|, and the response to a bounded input for marginal cases.
meta.problem: Why is the left half-plane the stable one — and what happens exactly on the boundary?
meta.theory:
$h(t)=\sum r_ke^{p_kt}$ (simple poles), so |h| grows or decays like $e^{\max\mathrm{Re}\,p\;t}$: ∫|h| < ∞ iff all Re p < 0, which is exactly BIBO stability. On the axis, a simple pole gives a
bounded but non-decaying h (∫|h| diverges), and a bounded input at the pole's frequency drives an unbounded output (resonance: t·sin ωt); a double pole on the axis gives
polynomial growth t^{m−1}.
meta.method:
Pole pairs at σ ± 2j for σ ∈ {−0.5, −0.1, 0, +0.1}; plus s = 0 simple and double. Impulse responses on 0–60 s; growth rate from a line fit of log of the local peak envelope;
∫₀ᵀ|h| as T grows; bounded input sin(2t) to the σ = 0 system.
